title: Natural Gas Prices Led Household Bill Increases in September 2026
description: In the Consumer Price Index for September 2026, natural gas prices were 5.0% higher than a year earlier, compared with 3.7% for all items.
keyTakeaways: Overall consumer prices were 3.7% higher in September 2026 than a year earlier (Billix calculation from BLS index values)[^1][^2].
Utility (piped) gas service rose the most of the household bills we track: +5.0%[^2].
3 of 6 bill types rose faster than overall prices[^2].

blocks.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics measures price changes for what households buy in the Consumer Price Index (CPI)[^1]. Comparing September 2026 with September 2025, using the U.S. city average indexes that are not seasonally adjusted (Billix calculation)[^2]:

blocks.caption: Change in prices, September 2025 to September 2026

blocks.text: The CPI tracks prices, not bills: what you pay also depends on how much you use and on fees and taxes where you live. Changes are rounded to one decimal place.

sections.heading: What it means for your bill

blocks.text: National averages are a yardstick, not the price you will pay. Your bill depends on your provider, your state and how much you use.
To check a bill line by line, start with the [bill guides](/categories).

Billix publishes this update automatically when the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the monthly Consumer Price Index. The numbers come straight from the agency's data service and the wording follows a fixed template, so nothing here is estimated or rewritten.
